Paragraph: When Prince Rama was told by Kaikeyi that he must forgo his coronation and go into forest exile for fourteen years, his expression did not change. He accepted the news with a gentle smile, comforting his distraught parents and stating that honoring his father's promise was his highest joy.
Situation/Problem_Faced: Sudden loss of status, unjust treatment, public rejection, and abrupt change in life plans.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: Rama practices complete acceptance (Prasada Buddhi), remaining calm and showing respect to those causing his exile.
Outcome/Resolution: By remaining undisturbed, Rama turns a personal catastrophe into a display of grace and moral triumph.

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Prasada Buddhi (Tranquil acceptance of life's events as divine order)
Samatva (Equanimity in praise and blame, gain and loss)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: Rama illustrates perfect equanimity, treating triumph and exile with equal calm.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: A model of radical acceptance, emotional composure, and freedom from entitlement.
